audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows disagreed with their own why-text: levels 4-5 and 6 read Skill while whys[3] says 'you out-trade him' and whys[4] says your ultimate holds through Subjugate; two items read Jax while whys[6] says he out-sustains the long fight and you should end fast. Separately, diff is FAV but report[14] and the tone colour call it an even matchup.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Jax/Jax/Jax/Jax/Jax/Skill at 54.83% over 518 games — a favoured lane with a long Jax window. The mirror (trundle__jax) already set its own side to HARD at 7/10, so this side must read as favoured to match.
audit.corrected: Rows set to Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Skill in both layers, ratings realigned to 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 6, 5; diffRating dropped to 4/10 with breakdown.difficulty, report[14] and the tone colour brought in line with diff FAV.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes were right but carried no cooldowns, so 'commit on his Subjugate cooldown' had nothing behind it.
audit.why: Subjugate is 120/100/80s and steals Health, Armor and MR immediately, doubling the stolen amount over the next 4 seconds — that doubling is why a fight that goes long swings to him. Your own ultimate is 110/100/90s, so at rank 1 he gets his back slightly slower than you do.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns now carry the 120s Subjugate and its doubling window.
sources: brief enemyKit R cd 120/100/80 and text

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (1) spikes[0] and wants.you[0] tell you Counter Strike dodges 'the swing off his Chomp bite' — the mirror audit concluded the opposite, that Chomp lands through Counter Strike while his plain autos do not. (2) Pillar of Ice creates real impassable terrain, which blocks Leap Strike, and that was buried in wants.foe rather than stated as an interaction.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges 'all incoming attacks', which is attacks, not ability casts, and Chomp is a cast (Riot: Trundle bites his opponent, dealing damage, slowing and sapping Attack Damage). The kit's derived autoReset flag is what produced the old claim; per the brief's own rule, where a derived flag and the description pull apart, the description wins. Pillar of Ice (21/19.5/18/16.5/15s, 1000 range) carries the terrain flag — it can wall your Leap Strike path outright. Chomp is only 3.5s, so it is never a window; Pillar and Subjugate are.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text and wants.you[0] now say Counter Strike blanks his autos while Chomp lands through; report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns state the Pillar terrain and its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Subjugate was the only tracked cooldown and had no number; Chomp at 3.5s was being treated as a punishable window when it never is.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice at 21s rank 1 is the cooldown that decides whether you can reach him at all.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten around Subjugate and Pillar of Ice.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Subjugate and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Subjugate and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Trundle carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Trundle carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Subjugate's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: You out-trade him as you rank the combo; his sustain is not online yet and his autos keep feeding your dodge-stun window.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Trundle's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Your R's Armor/MR active holds through Subjugate's resist-steal, and the on-hit ramp out-DPSes his King's Tribute drain.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Trundle carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Late, King's Tribute, stolen AD and Subjugate's doubling steal out-sustain a long fight — end it fast or splitpush.

edits.before: Steals your stats. Don’t fight into it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Subjugate is 120s at rank 1 and doubles its steal over 4s — open before it.

edits.before: - Trundle Subjugate: matchup-defining — Steals your stats. Don’t fight into it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Trundle Subjugate: 120/100/80s — steals Health, Armor and MR, and doubles it over 4s. Never open into it. - Pillar of Ice: 21s at rank 1, real terrain that blocks Leap Strike. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Trundle's Subjugate: Steals your stats. Don’t fight into it. When it is down — Q-E-W him.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice is real terrain — it blocks Leap Strike, so leap to a minion or hold Q to reposition.

edits.before: Counter Strike comes online and dodges Trundle's autos (including the auto-reset swing off his Chomp bite), then recasts to stun him — your first hard trade window.
edits.after: Counter Strike comes online and blanks Trundle's autos, though the Chomp bite itself is a cast and lands through it — recast to stun him for your first hard trade window.

edits.before: Hold Counter Strike through his autos and the swing off his Chomp bite, then recast to stun and burst
edits.after: Hold Counter Strike through his autos — Chomp still lands — then recast to stun and burst him down

notes: The Chomp-through-Counter-Strike point is Medium confidence, inherited from the mirror audit rather than independently provable: Riot's Counter Strike wording is 'dodge all incoming attacks', which reads as basic attacks, and Chomp is described as a cast — but the kit's derived autoReset flag points the other way and needsResearch is empty, so neither source settles it. I stated it the mirror's way so the two pages agree. Mirror also notes a win-rate source split (disk 45.17%/518 vs packet 45.75%/400 on their side); this side's packet reads 54.83%/518. Ability-name note: Data Dragon 16.15.1 calls Jax's R 'Grandmaster-at-Arms'; the stale 'Grandmaster's Might' remains in breakdown.late here and in fields I did not otherwise touch.
